name: Devoción (Downtown Brooklyn)
why_included: Couches, tables, plenty of outlets and plants; wifi weekdays only; spacious for groups.

name: Lincoln Station
why_included: Large center table popular with laptop users (group-friendly); open until 9pm.

name: Kona Coffee & Co. (2nd Ave)
why_included: Plenty of outlets, lots of space and light; some tables suit group work; WiFi limited on weekends.

name: Capital One Cafe (59th & Lexington)
why_included: Lots of seating, private call nooks, free WiFi, multiple bathrooms; group-friendly.

name: Capital One Cafe (Union Square)
why_included: Most outlets anywhere, multiple floors of booths, desks and armchairs, bookable nooks, no purchase needed; group-friendly.

name: Sweetleaf (Long Island City)
why_included: Quiet back laptop room; free wifi; reportedly no screens on weekends.

name: The Hoxton Williamsburg
why_included: Large lobby with vintage sofas, armchairs, two fireplaces; staff relaxed about people staying. Busy with freelancers; bar crowd later.

name: Jefferson Market Library
why_included: Landmark courthouse renovated 2022; second-floor Adult Reading Room for study; open to 8pm Mon-Thu.

name: 550 Madison Avenue Garden
why_included: Snohetta-redesigned covered garden (not fully enclosed); seating and benches throughout; open daily 7am-11pm year-round.

name: New York Public Library for the Performing Arts
why_included: Quiet research library at Lincoln Center; personal laptops allowed in reading rooms; pair with the Rubenstein Atrium next door.
